summary:
Radar for 2026-11-20 (GLP-1 focus). I checked 6 claims with searches; all candidates are below, best first.

The two biggest openings are both approved-drug news:
1. **Foundayo (orforglipron).** It was approved in Canada on Nov 18 and became prescribable in Australia this week (RACGP newsGP Nov 19, Medical Republic, AusDoc). That brings fresh searches from Canada and Australia onto a video that already gains about 30 minutes a day. Ship the queued Foundayo what-to-expect long video with the 11-20 fact-check fixes applied.
2. **The class-wide NAION eye warning.** It got a second mainstream wave (ABC News Nov 18, The Hill and News-Medical Nov 19, Denmark compensating 31 users). Verified numbers: the FDA reviewed 126 trials with more than 134,000 patients and found about 6.4 vs 3.8 events per 100,000 people per year. It fits the label-change format and gives the queued Serious Risks video a fresh hook.

**Holiday table: peak in 3–7 days.** The Conversation's doctor guide and Newswise's "Plate it safe" (both Nov 19) confirm it peaks around Nov 24–27. Keep the 20:00 holiday Shorts linked to Thanksgiving, including travelling with the pen.

**Stopping: still rising.** Healthline (Nov 19) and Men's Fitness (Nov 17) both covered it. Use it to drive the Side Effects → Stopping → Keeping Results links.

**Fast-turn option: SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS.** A randomized trial in JAMA (Nov 15): 160 teens aged 12–17 with obesity-related complications. BMI fell 18.5% on tirzepatide vs +0.5% on placebo, and 53.5% dropped below the obesity threshold. Rated caution because the audience is adults (pitch it to parents) and approval for teens is still pending.

**Search-demand formats, kept as required:**
- SURMOUNT-5: tirzepatide vs semaglutide, a randomized head-to-head
- pen how-to and injection sites, per the Instructions for Use
- pen travel and storage
- hair loss, nausea and injection-site Shorts
- long-term safety, as the Serious Risks video

**Folded into existing videos:** the Nature/ScienceDaily gene-variant story ("why they don't work for everyone") goes into Weight Loss in the Trials as a why-results-vary chapter. The Wegovy pill in Australia is a hook for a pills-vs-tirzepatide explainer, with a clear note that the trials can't be compared directly.

**Small or observational items (Shorts or chapters at most):** the prebiotic-soda GI pilot (80 people, likely industry-linked), the small UK nutrient-shortfall study, the semaglutide binge-eating RCT (sensitive subject), and the brain and memory headlines. None should be a topic on its own.

**Rejected:** employer coverage and cost, the "GLP-1 vacation", illegal online sales, the psychosis case reports after abrupt stopping, licensing and stock stories, and mouse studies.

I couldn't confirm the Washington Post weightlifting piece by search, so that candidate leans on T-REx and the New York Post gym story. For Foundayo in Canada I only found Lilly Canada's product page, not Health Canada's own notice, so cite CityNews or the PR Newswire release until the official listing is found.

Sources: [Pharmacy Times NAION](https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/fda-requires-class-wide-glp-1-ra-labeling-changes-for-potential-naion-risk), [Fox5 NAION explainer](https://www.fox5ny.com/news/what-is-naion-ozempic-wegovy-other-glp-1s-linked-rare-eye-condition), [AJMC SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS](https://www.ajmc.com/view/tirzepatide-lowers-bmi-by-185-in-adolescents-with-obesity), [Medical Daily teen side effects](https://www.medicaldaily.com/zepbound-teen-trial-bmi-reduction-side-effects-481289), [Lilly Canada Foundayo](https://medical.lilly.com/en-ca/products/foundayo), [ClinicalTrials.gov prebiotic soda pilot](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07744360), [Women's Weekly Wegovy pill AU](https://www.womensweekly.com.au/health/wegovy-weight-loss-pill-australia/).

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) and the class-wide NAION eye warning: what the new label wording says and how rare it is (FDA: about 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 per year)
candidates.angle: A calm label-change explainer. What NAION is in one sentence. The FDA's numbers: 126 trials, more than 134,000 patients, about 6.4 vs 3.8 events per 100,000 people per year. The one action the label asks for: report sudden, painless vision loss or visual-field changes right away. Name both NANOS and the AAO. Use it as the fresh hook for the queued 'Serious Risks: How Rare?' long video, and as an 08:00-style Short: 'Tirzepatide's new eye warning, in one number'. No standalone 'scary' line; put the relief fact in sentence 1. End with talk to your prescriber; never advise stopping.

The NAION Short did 471 views on TikTok, one of our best. Most coverage names semaglutide; few explainers lead with tirzepatide.
